item.title: Beyond the Signal: Four Remote Escapes for a Deeper Connection with Nature
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For travelers willing to venture beyond familiar routes and the reach of reliable connectivity, Untamed Travelling curates journeys into some of the world’s more remote wilderness landscapes. In northern India, Vanghat is a secluded eco-lodge on the Western Ramganga River, deep within the Corbett Tiger Reserve, reached by a cross-country hike or a combination of four-wheel drive and river raft. Farther north, a snow leopard expedition into Ladakh takes travelers into the Himalayas, with stays at Rumbak Wildlife Lodge on the edge of Hemis National Park. In East Africa, Alex Walker’s Serian offers intimate safari camps in the wilderness areas of Kenya and Tanzania, while South Africa’s Xaus Lodge places guests in the Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park, where individual chalets look directly onto the surrounding landscape. With limited or no connectivity at several of these properties, each experience offers a rare opportunity to step away from digital distractions and give the natural world undivided attention.

The Curated Take

There is a particular kind of extraordinary that only emerges when the familiar conveniences of travel fall away. A lodge reached by river, a mountain expedition in search of an elusive animal, or a night in the Kalahari beyond the reach of a phone signal asks something different of the traveler: patience, curiosity, and a willingness to be fully present. These destinations are not simply remote for the sake of distance. Their appeal lies in the access they offer to landscapes and wildlife that remain largely beyond the everyday frame of experience. In an increasingly connected world, the freedom to be unreachable may be one of travel’s most meaningful luxuries.

item.title: Saba: The Caribbean’s Quietest Kind of Escape
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Just five square miles in size, with a population of approximately 2,000, Saba offers a distinctly different perspective on Caribbean travel. Known as the “Unspoiled Queen of the Caribbean,” the small Dutch Caribbean island has resisted large-scale development, with just five hotels and approximately 140 guest rooms preserving a sense of intimacy rarely found elsewhere in the region. Its dramatic volcanic landscape encompasses 20 hiking trails, five distinct microclimates, and Mount Scenery, the highest point in the Kingdom of the Netherlands at 887 meters. Trails wind through lush rainforest, cloud-covered mountainsides, and changing landscapes, while the surrounding waters are protected as a marine park. In Windwardside, a charming village retains a strong local character, offering another way to experience an island whose appeal rests as much in its atmosphere as its natural beauty.

The Curated Take

Saba’s distinction is not simply that it is small, but that it has preserved the qualities that make a place feel like itself. There are no sprawling resort developments competing for attention, only a remarkable landscape, a close-knit community, and the freedom to experience the Caribbean at a different pace. For travelers accustomed to destinations defined by their amenities and activity, Saba offers another kind of discovery: the pleasure of finding a place where nature sets the rhythm and the absence of crowds becomes a luxury in its own right.

item.title: The Luxury of Stillness in North Carolina’s Blue Ridge Mountains
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In the Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina, Art of Living Retreat Center offers a different expression of luxury, one shaped by space, stillness, and a deeper connection to the natural world. Set amid mountain scenery and seasonal foliage, the retreat brings together immersive wellness programs in meditation, breathwork, silence, and Ayurvedic practices. Guests can step away from the pace of everyday life and enter experiences designed to encourage reflection, mindful movement, and a renewed awareness of the present. As interest in restorative travel grows, the center speaks to travelers seeking more than an escape: an opportunity to find perspective in the quiet rhythms of nature and in the simple act of being still.

The Curated Take

Not every extraordinary journey is measured by how far it takes a traveler or how much it allows them to see. Sometimes, its value lies in what falls away: the noise, the demands, and the constant pull of connectivity. Art of Living Retreat Center offers a compelling perspective on wellness travel, where the mountain landscape becomes part of the experience and stillness is not an absence of activity, but an invitation to pay closer attention. It is a reminder that restoration can be its own form of discovery.

item.title: Orient Express Corinthian Brings a New Era of Sailing Luxury to the Caribbean
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Following a transatlantic crossing from Lisbon via the Azores, Orient Express Corinthian has arrived in Bridgetown, Barbados, beginning a Caribbean season that will extend through the Bahamas and Florida before returning to Europe in spring 2027. The 220-meter sailing yacht will connect destinations including the British Virgin Islands, Anguilla, Saint Martin, Saint-Barthélemy, Antigua, Barbuda, Barbados and Puerto Rico through voyages designed to make the passage itself part of the experience. Its January itinerary from Saint Martin to San Juan, Puerto Rico, includes stops in St. Kitts and Nevis, Antigua, Anguilla and Virgin Gorda, home to the celebrated Baths. Designed by architect Maxime d’Angeac, the yacht features 54 suites with panoramic sea views and dedicated butler service, five restaurants overseen by 18-Michelin-starred chef Yannick Alléno, a Guerlain Spa, eight bars and a marina. Three SolidSail rigs, supported by hybrid LNG propulsion, bring an innovative approach to wind-powered luxury travel.

The Curated Take

There is a distinction between traveling through the Caribbean and experiencing it from the sea. A sailing journey offers a changing perspective on the region, connecting islands and coastlines through the passages between them rather than treating each destination as an isolated stop. With its combination of expansive suites, fine dining and advanced sailing technology, Orient Express Corinthian brings the romance of ocean travel into a contemporary luxury setting. Its arrival also signals a new chapter for the Caribbean’s luxury cruise landscape, where the vessel itself becomes as significant as the destinations along the way.

item.title: Six Senses Kanuhura: Finding the Maldives Beyond the Main Island
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In the Lhaviyani Atoll, Six Senses Kanuhura offers a peaceful island retreat with an appealing sense of space and possibility. Set amid lush tropical surroundings and white-sand beaches, the resort features understated beachfront and overwater villas built with natural materials, while two neighboring deserted islands provide opportunities to venture beyond the main property. Guests can explore uninhabited shores, snorkel vibrant coral reefs and enjoy personalized wellness rituals, with each experience encouraging a slower connection to the surrounding environment. For travelers seeking a quieter perspective on the Maldives, Kanuhura offers more than the familiar appeal of a private island stay. Its setting invites discovery through the natural landscape, the surrounding waters and the freedom to spend time at a different pace.

The Curated Take

The appeal of a remote island is often measured by what lies just beyond its shores. At Six Senses Kanuhura, access to two neighboring deserted islands adds an element of exploration to the traditional Maldivian retreat. The experience is less about filling each day with activity and more about having the freedom to follow the water, discover a quieter stretch of sand or simply enjoy the luxury of time.

item.title: In Krabi, the Artisans and Traditions of Koh Klang Come Into View
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
A short journey from the luxury of Phulay Bay, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve leads to Koh Klang, a traditional fishing village where local craftsmanship remains part of everyday life. Through the resort’s Krabi’s Real Touch experience, guests travel by long-tail boat through mangrove waterways before continuing by tuk-tuk through the car-free village, whose narrow lanes are not designed for conventional traffic. There, artisans demonstrate the craft of carving miniature long-tail boats from coconut shells and the intricate art of hand-painted batik. Guests are invited to try the techniques themselves, creating an opportunity to meet the makers and gain a closer appreciation for the skills behind these distinctive local traditions. The experience offers a different perspective on Krabi, extending beyond its celebrated beaches and limestone scenery to the communities and creative practices that shape southern Thailand’s cultural identity.

The Curated Take

Koh Klang offers a compelling reminder that cultural discovery does not always require traveling far from a luxury resort. Sometimes it begins with a boat ride into a neighboring community and the chance to learn directly from the people who keep its traditions alive. For travelers seeking a more meaningful connection to Krabi, this experience brings the region’s living craft heritage into focus.

item.title: Six Senses Laamu: Where Marine Conservation Becomes Part of the Maldives Experience
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Set within the remote Laamu Atoll, Six Senses Laamu offers an island retreat where barefoot luxury and marine conservation are closely connected. Surrounded by white-sand beaches, turquoise lagoons and thriving coral reefs, the resort’s beachfront and overwater villas are designed to blend with their natural surroundings. Its Maldives Underwater Initiative gives guests an opportunity to explore the marine environment alongside resident biologists, learning about ongoing efforts to protect sea turtles, manta rays and fragile reef ecosystems. These encounters add a meaningful dimension to a stay in the Indian Ocean, inviting travelers to look beyond the familiar pleasures of a tropical escape and develop a deeper understanding of the waters and wildlife that define this remote corner of the Maldives.

The Curated Take

The Maldives is often experienced from the surface, through overwater villas, turquoise lagoons and days spent on the beach. At Six Senses Laamu, the opportunity to learn from marine biologists offers another way to understand the destination. Conservation becomes part of the travel experience itself, giving a stay here a sense of purpose that extends beyond the beauty of the setting.

item.title: Twelve Travelers, 350 Residents: A Rare Encounter with East Greenland
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In East Greenland, where remote settlements exist within an immense Arctic landscape, the scale of an expedition can shape the experience as much as the destination itself. Secret Atlas, a polar expedition company specializing in small-ship journeys, brings groups of just 12 guests ashore at Ittoqqortoormiit, a community of approximately 350 residents founded in 1925 by 80 Inuit families. Visitors have the opportunity to meet local residents and learn about traditional carving, including tupilaks, spirit figures made from bone or tusk. The visit forms part of an expedition through Scoresbysund, the world’s largest fjord, reached by charter flight from Iceland. With itineraries adapted to changing ice and wildlife conditions and one polar guide for every six guests, the journey is designed around close observation and a measured presence in this remote environment. The small group size also allows for a more considered visit to a community where tourism remains on a very different scale from that of more frequently visited destinations.

The Curated Take

There is a meaningful distinction between reaching a remote place and experiencing it with care. In Ittoqqortoormiit, a landing by a dozen travelers offers a more intimate scale of encounter, while time with local residents brings human context to an otherwise extraordinary Arctic landscape. Secret Atlas’s approach speaks to a growing interest in expedition travel that values patience, small groups and respectful cultural exchange alongside wildlife and scenery.

item.title: Madagascar by Dugout Canoe: An Island Experience Rooted in Village Life
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
On Nosy Komba, off Madagascar’s northwest coast, Time + Tide Tsara Komba offers an intimate island stay shaped by its relationship with the neighboring community. The eight-room retreat shares its shoreline with a local village, creating opportunities for guests to experience daily life beyond the property. Guided walks and traditional dugout canoe journeys lead to Ampangorina and its market, while encounters with local fishing traditions offer a closer understanding of skills passed down through generations. Guests can also learn palangrotte fishing from a local guide, using a nylon line wrapped around a wooden plate in a technique that reflects the enduring connection between the island’s communities and the sea. The experience brings a cultural dimension to a stay in Madagascar’s Indian Ocean landscape, where the appeal extends beyond tropical scenery to the people and practices that give the island its character.

The Curated Take

The most meaningful island experiences often begin where the resort ends. On Nosy Komba, the opportunity to travel by dugout canoe, visit a village market and learn a traditional fishing technique offers a more grounded understanding of Madagascar. It is a reminder that a destination’s character is found not only in its landscapes, but in the knowledge and traditions sustained by the communities who call it home.

item.title: Trinidad & Tobago Beyond the Beach: Discovering the Island Nation’s Cultural and Natural Character
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For travelers accustomed to thinking of the Caribbean primarily in terms of beaches and resort stays, Trinidad & Tobago offers a more layered perspective on the region. Through its HADCO Experiences portfolio and Mt Plaisir Estate Hotel, the destination invites exploration of a quieter side of the islands, where natural landscapes, local traditions and cultural character help shape the travel experience. The property’s introduction points toward a style of Caribbean travel that places greater emphasis on discovering the destination itself rather than remaining within a conventional beach-focused escape. For those seeking a more immersive understanding of Trinidad & Tobago, it offers a starting point for considering the country’s distinctive identity and the experiences that set it apart within the wider Caribbean.

The Curated Take

Trinidad & Tobago occupies a distinctive place in the Caribbean, with a cultural identity and natural character that extend well beyond the region’s familiar beach narrative. The opportunity here is to approach the destination with curiosity, allowing its traditions, landscapes and local character to guide the experience. More property and destination details would help bring the story into sharper focus, but the broader editorial angle is compelling: a Caribbean escape defined by discovery rather than the shoreline alone.
